{{Quote|You will go to the Dagobah system. There you will learn from Yoda, the Jedi Master who instructed me.|[[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]]|<ref name="Episode 5">{{Film|V}}</ref>}}
The title of '''Jedi Master''' was the highest formal rank obtainable by a [[Jedi/Legends|member]] of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]]. Reserved for those who had shown exceptional devotion and skill as well as balance in [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] and often [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|combat]], only individuals who had been given the rank of Master could sit on the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi High Council]], with few exceptions (such as the case of [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] or [[Ki-Adi-Mundi/Legends|Ki-Adi-Mundi]]), or any of the three other [[Jedi Council/Legends|Councils]].<ref name="TJP" />

==Overview==
[[File:Jedi_Master_Belth_Allusis.jpg|thumb|left|220px|[[Belth Allusis]], esteemed Jedi Master during the [[Great Galactic War]]]]

The rank of Jedi Master was bestowed upon very few Jedi Knights in every generation. As such, Jedi Masters made up the smallest percent of the Order's membership. The most common path to this rank was to train and elevate several [[Padawan/Legends|Padawans]] to the rank of [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]], typically one right after the other, and have them all successfully pass their [[Jedi Trials/Legends|Jedi Trials]]. If one did not wish to train several students, a Jedi Knight could choose to undergo a modified version of the Trials of Knighthood or gain attention for their service to the Republic. Each of these feats could gain the Jedi High Council's acknowledgment and result in a promotion to the rank of Jedi Master.<ref name="TJP" /> When [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] [[New Jedi Order|reformed]] the Order following the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]], he promoted his students to the rank of Jedi Master based on their degree of mastery of the Force. As the order began to grow, most Jedi Knights were promoted to the rank of Jedi Master based on the extraordinary deeds they performed for the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]]. One well-known example was the promotion of Jedi Knight [[Kyle Katarn]] following the defeat of the [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Desann]] at his blade.<ref name="Star Wars: Jedi Knight II: Jedi Outcast">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight II: Jedi Outcast]]''</ref>

A practice strongly discouraged by the Jedi High Council and little seen during the [[Golden Age of the Old Republic]] was a Jedi Knight judging themselves and assuming the rank of Master without the Jedi Council's approval. This was not uncommon practice during the [[Old Sith Wars|Old]] and [[New Sith Wars]], as the order was not centrally controlled during the period, and many saw their victories against the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] a sign of their skills and achievements.<ref name="TJP" /> One well-known example of this practice was the ascension to mastery by Jedi [[Jorus C'baoth]];<ref name="Dark Force Rising">''[[Dark Force Rising]]''</ref> indeed even his clone, [[Joruus C'baoth]], would also claim himself a Jedi Master.<ref name="Heir to the Empire">''[[Heir to the Empire]]''</ref> Luke Skywalker was forced to promote himself to the rank of Jedi Master; due to the fact that there were no known Jedi Masters left alive to officially grant him the rank.<ref name="Jedi Search">''[[Jedi Search]]''</ref>

Those Jedi Masters whose talents were extremely superior were asked to join the ranks of the Jedi Councils. Their promotion was often based on their specialized knowledge or skill sets, or vast experience in the field. As a member of a Jedi Council, a Jedi Master was given great responsibility within the Order, and often was seen at the Coruscant Temple or satellite facility instructing Initiates in the basics of the Order's techniques. The members of the Jedi Council were not necessarily the most skilled lightsaber duelist or even those possessed of the greatest range of Force powers. Instead, membership was reserved to those Jedi Masters who could see through a situation or add insight the best swordsmen could not ever perceive.<ref name="TJP" />

The Jedi Knight [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] was never granted the rank of Jedi Master - despite the [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] special appointment of him to the Jedi High Council during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], something that had never been done in the history of the order.<ref name="ROTS">{{Film|III}}</ref> Other Jedi Masters; such as [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] were members of what was known as the [[Old Guard]] or those Jedi that were under consideration for appointment to one of the Jedi Councils.<ref name="Rise">''[[Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader]]''</ref> However, some members considered Master Jinn too radical to sit on the esteemed body.<ref name="Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace">{{Film|I}}</ref>

[[File:JKA_jedimaster.png|thumb|right|250px|A Jedi Master of the reformed Jedi Order.]]

While Jedi Master was the highest of the formal ranks of the order, the Jedi High Council would select a Jedi Master who possessed the strongest mind, the greatest leadership qualities and incomparable mastery of the Force and name them [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]], the undisputed leader of the order. In the order's earliest years, several Grand Masters were appointed, though this practice was abandoned following the [[Ruusan Reformations/Legends|Ruusan Reformation]]. In addition to the Grand Master rank, the Jedi High Council and the [[Council of First Knowledge/Legends|Council of First Knowledge]] appointed a leader to guide discussion and moderate debates. In the case of the Jedi High Council, the [[Master of the Order/Legends|Master of the Order]] was a rank often held by the Grand Master himself. The First Knowledge Council was led by the [[Caretaker of First Knowledge/Legends|Caretaker]]; who at one point shared the title of [[Lore Keeper|Chief Librarian]] of the [[Librarian's Assembly]].<ref name="TJP" />

While there were generally no locks at the Temple on Coruscant, a few chambers were sealed to non-Jedi Masters. The [[Holocron Vault/Legends|Holocron Vaults]] in the [[Jedi Archives/Legends|Jedi Archives]] were sealed off to all but members of the Jedi High Council, as was the [[Treasury room|Treasury]] located under the [[Jedi Council Chamber/Legends|High Council Chamber]]. This was to ensure that the treasures of the order; especially the dangerous [[Sith holocron/Legends|Sith holocrons]] found in the Archives Vaults; did not fall into the wrong hands.<ref name="TJP" />
